headline: BEST-EVER COPPER-GOLD INTERCEPT: Abitibi Metals Drills 4.04% CuEq Over 14m at B26, Quebec
snippet: Abitibi Metals (CSE: AMQ) delivered its strongest copper-gold intersection yet at B26 in western Quebec — 4.04% CuEq over 14 metres within a wider 46.7-metre zone grading 1.48% CuEq at 946m depth. The high-grade core exceeds current block model grades and continues to expand the Discovery Silver-backed project's high-grade copper-gold domain.

headline: MINERA ALAMOS PULLS TRIGGER: $58M Copperstone Arizona Gold Mine Approved — 303 Koz at 4.87 g/t, June Start
snippet: Minera Alamos (TSXV: MAI) greenlit construction of the Copperstone underground gold mine in Arizona after a positive pre-feasibility study — $58M capex, 303 koz proven and probable reserves at 4.87 g/t gold, 1.2-year payback at $3,500/oz. Engineering and procurement begin June 2026; first production targets mid-2027, doubling the company's current annual output.

headline: COBRE PANAMA DECISION DAY: Government Releases Long-Awaited Audit of First Quantum's Shut-Down Copper Mine
snippet: Panama is releasing the final third-party audit of First Quantum Minerals' (TSX: FM) Cobre Panama copper mine as anti-mining protests re-emerge. President Mulino will decide the mine's fate once the government reviews the findings — a pivotal moment for one of the world's largest copper operations, shut down since late 2023 after a Supreme Court constitutional ruling.

headline: GOLD SLIPS to $4,470, Two-Month Low — Iran Ceasefire Talks and Inflation Fears Chip the Safe-Haven Bid
snippet: Gold fell near $4,400 Thursday — its weakest level in two months — as a US-Iran 60-day ceasefire memorandum reduced safe-haven demand while sticky energy inflation capped the rebound. Analysts see June holding a $4,300–$4,725 range unless a major catalyst arrives; gold is still up 35% year-over-year.

headline: Silver at $77 Eyes $80 Breakout as Sixth Straight Deficit Has Drained 762 Million Oz From Global Vaults
snippet: Silver is holding channel support near $77 with a technical setup targeting $80.69, backed by the Silver Institute's confirmed sixth consecutive annual supply deficit. Since 2021, cumulative drawdowns have removed 762 million ounces from above-ground inventories, with solar panel manufacturing and AI hardware demand absorbing supply faster than global mines can replenish it.

headline: Newmont Minted $7.3B Free Cash Flow in 2025 — But SSR Mining's $1.5B Copler Windfall May Be the Better Entry
snippet: Motley Fool pits the world's largest gold miner against a leaner repositioning play: Newmont set a record $7.3B in free cash flow in 2025 and returned $3.4B to shareholders, while SSR Mining trades at a cheaper forward multiple and is set to bank $1.5B from selling its troubled Çöpler mine. The case for SSR rests on strategic repositioning and re-rating potential.

headline: 9.92 g/t GOLD in 92 Metres: South Pacific Metals Hits K92 Mining's Papua New Guinea Corridor in Maiden Drill
snippet: South Pacific Metals (TSX-V: SPMC) intersected 92 metres of gold-copper mineralization at Ontenu NE in Papua New Guinea's Kainantu Transfer Zone, with peak re-assays of 9.92 g/t gold and 2.35% copper in maiden drilling. The Osena project borders K92 Mining's high-grade underground operation — a corridor with an established discovery track record.

headline: SSR MINING EXITS TURKEY for $1.5B: Copler Sale Creates $1.6B Net Cash Platform, Americas-Only Focus
snippet: SSR Mining (NASDAQ: SSRM) is selling its 80% stake in the troubled Çöpler mine in Türkiye to Cengiz Holding for $1.5 billion cash, expected to close before end of Q3 2026. The deal removes the mine where a 2024 fatal accident triggered permanent shutdown, leaving SSR with $1.6B net cash and a strategically cleaner Americas-only production profile as a potential re-rating catalyst.

headline: Uranium Holds $85/lb as AI Data Center Build-Out Adds Structural Demand Layer to Tight Nuclear Market
snippet: Uranium spot prices held near $85 per pound in late May — down from a January high of $101 but still 18% above year-ago levels. Long-term contracting demand is at record highs as the AI infrastructure buildout joins nuclear plant restarts as new demand drivers. Kazatomprom forecasts a structural market deficit reaching 21 million pounds by 2030.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH GRIP HOLDS Post-Trump-Xi Summit: Key Exports Still at 41-49% of Pre-Control Volumes
snippet: China's rare earth export controls remain firmly in place following the May 14-15 Trump-Xi summit, with exports of key heavy rare earths running at just 41-49% of pre-restriction volumes according to Benchmark Minerals Intelligence. Despite White House language about China 'addressing' supply concerns, no binding deal or timeline emerged — keeping Western manufacturers on a tight leash.
